title: Calibration and experimental verification of discrete element simulation parameters of seedling pot based on NSGA-II algorithm
content:
by Dong Ji, Jia Shi, Zhu Zhao, Fengbo Liu, Chenghu Guo, Yongqi Wang, Subo Tian

To improve the accuracy of the simulation parameters used in discrete element simulations of transplanting operations and to facilitate further optimization of key transplanter components, this study calibrated and optimized the discrete element model of the seedling pot (16 × 8 holes) based on puncture and shear tests. The contact parameters of the seedling pot were determined through basic tests. The Plackett-Burman test was used to select the initial parameters and determine their value ranges. The shear strength (X2), the static friction coefficient (X4), and the ultimate stress (X10) significantly affected the puncture and shear forces. Based on the central composite design (CCD), a two-objective (puncture force and shear force) regression model was established, and the optimal values were obtained with Design-Expert software. When X2, X4, and X10 were 1.4, 0.885, and 0.115, respectively, the predicted puncture and shear forces were 6.4 N and 11.62 N. Compared with the measured values (6.4 N and 11.3 N), the software solution emphasized the puncture force. The parameters were then substituted into EDEM (2022, Altair Engineering Inc., Troy, MI, USA) for simulation, giving simulation values of 7.2 N and 10.1 N. The relative errors with respect to the measured values were 12.5% and 10.6%, respectively. The calculation has defects. In this study, the multi-objective optimization based on NSGA-II algorithm was applied to the EDEM parameter model. A set of optimized Pareto optimal solutions were selected and simulated. The relative errors of the resulting model were small, namely 6.25% and 7.08%. The results indicate the potential feasibility of the NSGA-II calibration method under the investigated conditions.
